newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday November 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday November 27.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi denies a conflict of interest over charges requested against him by a magistrate over alleged irregularities during his chairmanship of state industrial holding IRI. Asked whether he might resign if ordered to stand trial he answered "It's a hypothesis that I am not raising because there is no element that could suggest going to trial" (all).
* Massimo D'Alema leader of the PDS party, the major party in the centre-left coalition government, said that if the government fell then new elections would be needed (all).

* Tension seems to be easing between the ruling coalition and the centre-right opposition as the government says it is ready to review the one-off Eurotax linked to the 1997 budget. But Oliviero Diliberto, leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation party in the lower house, says "if something changes, then we should rediscuss the whole issue" (all).
* Labour minister Tiziano Treu says talks on pension reforms should be anticipated in 1997 instead of 1998 as was initially planned. But trade unions disagree (all).

* Speaking in the upper house, Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Italy should not slow down in its effort to reduce the public debt, as getting into the ERM "is a very different thing from joining EMU" (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* One-year Italian treasury bonds BOT yield fell under 6 percent to 5.75 percent at the last auction, the lowest level since the 1960's (Il Sole 24 Ore, La Stampa).

* Information technology group Olivetti said its net financial debt at the end of October was 3.028 trillion lire from 3.016 trillion lire at the end of September. The group added that it had decided to dissolve its powerful decision-making excutive committee, which included chairman Antonio Tesone, chief executive Roberto Colaninno, Rodolfo De Benedetti (son of ex-chairman Carlo De Benedetti), Franco Girard and German banker Peter Reimpell (all).
* Giorgio Fossa, chairman of employers association Confindustria, says "the lira re-entry into the ERM makes sense only if the discount rate is cut" (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
